data.name: Smart Contract Platform
data.content: Smart contract platforms are usually blockchains that host smart contracts or decentralized applications. Users can interact with different smart contracts on these platforms to perform various actions such as lending and borrowing funds, staking their assets or minting NFTs. Smart contracts are programs that are stored on the blockchain and are automatically executed when certain conditions are met.

data.name: Layer 1 (L1)
data.content: Layer 1 serves as the primary and autonomous chain on which transactions are directly executed and confirmed, as well as providing the essential infrastructure for the blockchain network.

data.name: Proof of Work (PoW)

data.name: Proof of Stake (PoS)
data.content: Proof of Stake (PoS) is a blockchain consensus mechanism where validators are selected to create new blocks based on the amount of cryptocurrency they hold and are willing to stake as collateral.

data.name: Stablecoins
data.content: A stablecoin is a type of cryptocurrency that is designed to maintain a stable value by being pegged to an external reference, such as a fiat currency.

data.name: USD Stablecoin
data.content: A USD stablecoin is a type of cryptocurrency that is designed to maintain a stable value by being pegged to the United States dollar.

data.name: Fiat-backed Stablecoin
data.content: A fiat-backed stablecoin is designed to maintain a stable value by being pegged to a reserve of fiat currency, such as the US dollar, euro, or other national currencies.

data.name: Made in USA
data.content: Refers to cryptocurrencies that have significant connections to the United States, either through their founding team or company headquarters.

data.name: Exchange-based Tokens
data.content: These tokens are associated with both centralized and decentralized exchanges which share the same purposes such as enjoy discounted trading fees and gain access to exclusive token sales on the exchange. While decentralized exchanges tokens also function as governance as a governance tokens, centralized exchange token does not.

data.name: Made in China

data.name: Alleged SEC Securities
data.content:
Tokens and cryptocurrencies alleged to be securities by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

data.name: Centralized Exchange (CEX) Token
data.content: These utility tokens are issued by a centralized exchange and can be used for a variety of purposes. Although holders are not able to exercise governance, they still carry many other benefits such as enjoy discounted trading fees and gain access to exclusive token sales on the exchange.

data.name: MiCA-Compliant Stablecoin
data.content: Fiat-backed stablecoins that are fully authorized under the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation. These assets are issued by regulated entities such as Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) or licensed credit institutions and adhere to strict European standards regarding 1:1 liquid reserve backing, transparent public auditing, and safeguarded custody to ensure consumer protection and financial stability.

data.name: GENIUS Act Compliant Stablecoin
data.content: Fiat-pegged stablecoins legally authorized and issued under the federal Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act) framework.

data.name: Real World Assets (RWA)
data.content: Real World Assets (RWAs) refer to tangible or physical assets that have value in the real world. The tokenization of RWAs involves representing these assets digitally on a blockchain, allowing for fractional ownership, increased liquidity, and more efficient management and trading of these assets.

data.name: Decentralized Finance (DeFi)
data.content: Decentralized Finance, is a financial system that operates without central authorities or intermediaries, using blockchain technology and smart contracts to provide a range of financial services such as lending, borrowing, and trading.

data.name: CoinList Launchpad

data.name: Governance

data.name: Meme

data.name: Decentralized Exchange (DEX)
data.content: Decentralized exchanges (DEXs) allow users to trade with one another in a permissionless manner and without any intermediaries.

data.name: Tokenized Private Credit
data.content: Tokenized private credit refers to the digital representation of economic claims on non-publicly traded debt instruments, such as direct loans to businesses or consumers.

data.name: Artificial Intelligence (AI)
data.content: Artificial Intelligence (AI) tokens are cryptocurrencies that power AI-related projects, such as AI-powered portfolio management, image generation, path finding, and more.

data.name: Infrastructure

data.name: Perpetuals

data.name: Privacy Coins
data.content: Cryptocurrencies designed primarily to function as digital cash or a store of value. Their architecture prioritizes the anonymity of the sender, receiver, and amount. They do not support general-purpose smart contracts or a dApp ecosystem.

data.name: Derivatives
data.content: Derivatives are financial instruments whose value is derived from an underlying asset (e.g. Crude Oil, Gold, Bitcoin etc). Compared to spot markets where the underlying asset changes ownership, in derivatives markets, traders trade contracts rather than the actual assets.

data.name: 4chan-Themed
data.content: 4chan-themed coins are tokens inspired by 4chan’s meme culture.

data.name: Zero Knowledge (ZK)
data.content:
Zero-knowledge proof or Zero-knowledge protocol is a method by which one party (the prover) can prove to another party (the verifier) that a given statement is true while the prover avoids conveying any additional information apart from the fact that the statement is indeed true.

This category tracks cryptocurrency that utilises Zero Knowledge implementation to execute transactions, which may include smart contract execution, value transfer, and others.

data.name: Elon Musk-Inspired
data.content: Meme coins inspired by Elon Musk, none of these projects are (necessarily) endorsed or created by Elon Musk.

data.name: Privacy Infrastructure
data.content: Protocols, networks, and developer tools designed to enable programmable privacy and confidential computation for decentralized applications. Unlike traditional 'Privacy Coins' which focus solely on transactional anonymity, these projects provide the infrastructure for encrypted smart contracts, private state management, and blind computation. They utilize advanced cryptography such as Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs), Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), and Multi-Party Computation (MPC) to allow developers to build complex applications where data is processed without being publicly revealed.

data.name: Gambling (GambleFi)
data.content: GambleFi refers to decentralized gambling platforms and tokens leveraging blockchain technology and smart contracts.

data.name: RWA Protocol
data.content: RWA Protocol refer to protocol that facilitates the tokenization of real-world assets.

data.name: Chain Abstraction
data.content: Chain abstraction is the concept of creating a seamless, unified user experience across multiple blockchains, allowing users and developers to interact with different chains without needing to manually bridge assets, switch networks, or handle chain-specific complexities.

data.name: Quantum-Resistant
data.content: Quantum-resistant projects are characterised by their use of post-quantum cryptographic algorithms (e.g., hash-based, lattice-based) to remain secure against potential attacks from future quantum computers.

data.name: YZi Labs (Prev. Binance Labs) Portfolio
data.content: Protocols and tokens that YZi Labs (Prev. Binance Labs) have invested in.

data.name: Options
data.content: Options refer to financial instruments that give holders the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell a cryptocurrency at a predetermined price, known as the strike price, before a specific date, known as the expiry date.

data.name: Prediction Markets
data.content: A crypto prediction market is a marketplace where people can bet on the outcome of future events using crypto.

data.name: Tokenized Treasuries
data.content: Tokenized Treasuries feature blockchain-native representations of marketable sovereign debt including T-bills, T-notes, and T-bonds that offer 24/7 on-chain access to yields through regulated, asset-backed tokens.

data.name: Cross-chain Communication
data.content: Cross-chain communication allows different blockchain networks to interact and exchange data and assets.

data.name: Oracle
data.content: Oracles are used by protocols in their smart contracts in order to obtain external data. This allows the closed-off blockchain environment to communicate with data points on the outside world. For example, a protocol offering synthetic Nasdaq-listed stock on the blockchain will need to pull external data from the stock market. With an oracle, the protocol will be able to do so.

data.name: x402 Ecosystem
data.content: x402 is an open protocol that defines an internet-native micropayment rail using HTTP 402 and stablecoins. It allows automated clients and AI agents to pay directly for APIs, data, and compute on demand, enabling real-time, low-friction transactions without intermediaries.

data.name: Layer 2 (L2)
data.content: Layer 2s are off-chain vertical scaling solutions that run on top of Layer 1 blockchains like Ethereum to improve scalability, while maintaining the decentralization and security standards of the Layer 1.

data.name: DePIN
data.content: DePIN refers to Decentralized Physical Infrastructure Networks which utilize blockchain and tokenized incentives to build real-world infrastructure across areas like wireless networks, storage, geolocation, transportation and energy.

data.name: Yield Farming
data.content: Yield farming involves putting cryptocurrency into a DeFi protocol to collect interest on trading fees. Liquidity providers can profit by providing liquidity in DeFi protocols like Uniswap, utilizing assets that would otherwise sit idle on an exchange or hot wallet.

data.name: Trump-Affiliated
data.content: This category includes tokens that are officially launched, endorsed, or held by Donald Trump or his immediate family. Only tokens with verifiable affiliation through official statements or reputable sources are included. Community-created tokens or projects that use Trump-related names or slogans without formal connection are excluded.

data.name: Stablecoin Issuer
data.content: Stablecoin issuers are protocols that create and manage stablecoins pegged to assets like fiat by using on-chain mechanisms such as collateralization, liquidity pools, or algorithmic supply adjustments.

data.name: Privacy Blockchain
data.content: Programmable Layer 1 or Layer 2 networks that serve as platforms for dApps while prioritizing confidentiality. Unlike standard, general-purpose programmable blockchains like Ethereum, these networks have privacy preserved at the consensus or execution layer, enabling "private-by-default" or "opt-in private" smart contracts.

data.name: Tokenized Commodities
data.content: Tokenized Commodities refers to digital representation of commodities such as oil, gold, silver on a blockchain platform.

data.name: Automated Market Maker (AMM)
data.content: Automated market makers (AMMs) make use of liquidity pools containing 2 or more assets, and prices are derived based on the proportion of each asset in that pool as well as the mathematical function used. Orders through an AMM are executed automatically via a smart contract that will calculate the trade prices algorithmically, including any slippage from the trade execution.

data.name: Tokenized Gold
data.content: Tokenized gold refers to digital representation of physical gold on a blockchain platform. These tokens are backed by an equivalent amount of real gold held in custody by the issuing institution.

data.name: Binance Launchpool
data.content: Tokens and coins launched on Binance Launchpool, a platform that allows crypto holders to earn new tokens by locking some of their existing assets.

data.name: Bitcoin Fork
data.content: A Bitcoin fork is a change to the underlying rules of the Bitcoin network that results in a split into a separate versions of the blockchain.

data.name: Crypto-backed Stablecoin
data.content: A crypto-backed stablecoin is designed to maintain a stable value by being backed by a reserve of other cryptocurrencies.

data.name: NFT
data.content: Non-fungible tokens (NFTs) are collectible elements that represent something unique and therefore are not mutually interchangeable. In other words, no non-fungible token is the same. NFT creators can also encrypt details such as rich metadata or secure file links allowing people to create all sorts of digital assets which are verifiable such as videos and songs.

data.name: Lending/Borrowing Protocols
data.content: Lending/borrowing protocols allow users to offer crypto loans by staking their assets in them without the need for a bank account. Users are given rewards, usually in the form of the protocol’s native token.

data.name: Index Coop Defi Index

data.name: Tokenized Money Market Fund (MMFs)
data.content: Tokens that represent shares or units (1:1) of a regulated money market fund, issued or recorded on-chain by a regulated entity. The token is yield-bearing, passing through the fund's NAV and returns via accumulating or distributing share classes.

data.name: Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)
data.content: A DAG-based blockchain is a type of distributed ledger that uses a graph-like structure instead of a linear chain, allowing faster and parallel transaction processing by linking each transaction to multiple previous ones.

data.name: Layer 0 (L0)
data.content: Layer 0 is the foundational infrastructure upon which multiple Layer 1 blockchains can be built.

data.name: Launchpad
data.content: Launchpad is a platform for crypto projects to hold Initial DEX Offerings (IDOs). Participants are able to gain early access to public and special token sales on the platform.

data.name: Gaming (GameFi)

data.name: Crypto Card Issuer
data.content: Tokens and cryptocurrencies representing platforms, centralized exchanges, or protocols that issue physical or virtual crypto debit and credit cards.

data.name: Data Availability
data.content: Data availability on the blockchain ensures that all participants have the transaction data needed to verify blocks, even with resource limitations and scalability needs. Without it, independent verification crumbles, compromising the entire system. Data availability centric protocols aim to allow nodes to verify data availability more efficiently.

data.content: Storage protocols allow users to store their data on the blockchain network in a decentralized manner. In return for operating a masternode, the operator is rewarded with the native currency.

data.name: Bank-Issued Stablecoin
data.content: Fiat-pegged stablecoins issued by a regulated bank or a bank's dedicated subsidiary, structured as a claim on a segregated reserve pool or as electronic money but not as a bank deposit. data.name: Fantom Ecosystem
data.content:
FANTOM is a new DAG-based smart contract platform that intends to solve the scalability issues of existing public distributed ledger technologies.
The platform intends to distinguish itself from the traditional block ledger-based storage infrastructure by attempting to employ an improved version of existing DAG-based protocols. Fantom adopts a new protocol known as the “Lachesis Protocol” to maintain consensus. This protocol is intended to be integrated into the Fantom Opera Chain. The aim is to allow applications built on Fantom to enjoy instant transactions and near zero transaction costs for all users.

data.name: Gnosis Chain Ecosystem
data.content: Formerly the xDai Chain, The Gnosis chain is a Layer 2 scaling solution for Ethereum but uses a different consensus algorithm - Proof of Stake (PoS) and Proof of Stake DAO (POSDAO). It is designed to be more efficient than Ethereum, with higher transaction throughput (70 transactions/second) and has a much lower transaction fee.

data.name: Near Protocol Ecosystem
data.content: NEAR is a sharded, developer-friendly, proof-of-stake public blockchain. It is designed to compete with Ethereum by providing a similar experience with decentralized applications and smart contracts, but with lower fees and higher throughput. The blockchain’s native token, NEAR, is used to pay for transactions and storing data on the blockchain. Smart contract developers receive a portion of the transaction fees generated by their contracts, while the remainder is burnt. This creates deflationary pressure on NEAR, making it more valuable as more transactions are performed.

data.name: Polygon Ecosystem
data.content: Polygon, formerly known as Matic, was originally meant to be a Layer-2 scaling solution for Ethereum to improve transaction throughput and speed. However, it has since become more popular as a stand-alone blockchain, with its own native projects and decentralized applications. Major DeFi protocols such as Aave and Curve have also found second homes on Polygon. Unlike Ethereum, Polygon operates on Proof-of-Stake (PoS) in which network participants can stake the network’s native MATIC tokens to validate transactions and participate in voting and other governance decisions. Polygon also hosts its own bridge that allows users to transfer assets from Ethereum to Polygon and vice versa.

data.name: Terra Ecosystem
data.content: Terra is a blockchain network that builds on the Tendermint consensus (Proof-of-Stake) and the Cosmos SDK toolkit. Terra’s network token is LUNA which powers the entire ecosystem. Unlike most blockchains, Terra’s ecosystem includes a native algorithmic stablecoin, TerraUSD (UST). A decentralized network with its own decentralized currency is a very attractive thesis for both users and developers. More dApps are being built on Terra, especially DeFi protocols which are now commonly known as TeFi.

data.name: Avalanche Ecosystem
data.content: Avalanche is a smart contract platform that allows users to create their own multi-purpose blockchains or decentralized applications (dApps). Their mainnet was launched in September 2020 and has since become a major hub of activity for DeFi and NFTs. In 2021, they announced their Avalanche Rush incentives program to introduce more applications and to promote further growth of their ecosystem. The Avalanche chain is centered around 3 main blockchains - the P-Chain, X-Chain and C-Chain. The C-Chain is Avalanche’s EVM implementation, which hosts various applications and smart contracts. Users can access Avalanche through centralized exchanges, the official Avalanche bridge or via Celer’s cBridge.

data.name: Solana Ecosystem
data.content: Solana is a general purpose blockchain similar to Ethereum. The underlying architecture is different, such that developers have to write applications using Rust instead of Solidity or Vyper. However, this may soon change with the introduction of the Neon EVM solution on Solana. End user applications as of now include decentralized finance (DeFi), non-fungible tokens (NFT), marketplaces, games, and more. One of its biggest features is its scalability in which Solana is able to process over 700,000 transactions per second. Its high throughput capability appeals to high frequency traders, which is spearheaded by FTX and Alameda Research. The first use case for DeFi applications on Solana is Serum, built by the team behind FTX.

data.name: Cosmos Ecosystem
data.content: Cosmos focuses on blockchain interoperability, working towards the vision of building the “Internet of Blockchains.”

data.name: BNB Chain Ecosystem
data.content:
BNB Chain is an alternative blockchain that is similar to Ethereum, capable of hosting smart contracts and decentralized applications. It was launched by Binance in September 2020 as the Binance Smart Chain, and relaunched in Feburary 2022 as BNB Chain. BNB uses the Proof-of-Staked-Authority model which has allowed for low transaction fees and higher throughput. 

Compared to Ethereum which would usually cost hundreds to make a few transactions, BNB only charges less than a few dollars. BNB supports the BEP-20 token format, which is essentially the same format as ERC-20 but on a different chain, and transaction fees are paid in Binance’s native exchange token, BNB.

data.name: Polkadot Ecosystem
data.content: Polkadot is a blockchain protocol designed to support multiple purpose-built blockchains under one unified network. Polkadot’s infrastructure begins with the relay chain, which acts as the central chain. Each chain that runs on Polkadot is called a parachain as they run parallel to the main relay chain, and is built on top of the relay chain. Besides parachains, projects can participate in the Polkadot ecosystem for a shorter fixed period of time through parathreads. Blockchains built on top of Polkadot’s own relay chain are also interoperable with blockchains that have vastly different technology stacks such as Ethereum and Bitcoin through bridges.
